answers.projectIdea:
I’m building Syncora, an enterprise-style collaboration and productivity platform that brings projects, teams, tasks, communication, and workflows together in one place.

I built the frontend with Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS, focusing on reusable components, responsive layouts, interactive dashboards, navigation, forms, filtering, and a polished UI/UX. As the project grew, I also worked on organizing the app so the features stayed maintainable instead of turning into a bunch of disconnected pages.

One of the biggest challenges was designing a large app with lots of connected features while keeping everything consistent and responsive. It pushed me to think beyond individual components and learn more about component architecture, state management, reusable design systems, responsive design, accessibility, and user experience.
answers.motivation:
I want to build CCC because I learn best by building and shipping, not by only discussing ideas or attending sessions.

While working on projects like Syncora, I’ve realized that the most valuable learning happens when I have to turn an idea into an actual working product—making decisions, debugging, iterating on the UI, using AI tools effectively, and dealing with problems that don’t have a predefined answer.

A conventional college club can provide exposure and networking, but CCC’s “no slides, ship every week” approach matches how I want to grow. I want to be around people who are actively building, experimenting, breaking things, and learning from what they ship.

I also don’t want to join CCC just as a participant. I want to help build the community itself—create projects, help other students turn ideas into working prototypes, and contribute to a culture where execution matters more than titles or certificates.

answers.experience:
I currently use Gemini Antigravity as my primary AI-assisted coding environment while building Syncora. I use LLMs to help with code generation, debugging, refactoring, understanding unfamiliar concepts, improving UI/UX, and exploring different implementation approaches.

My workflow is iterative: I break a feature into smaller requirements, use AI to accelerate implementation, review and test the generated code, identify issues, and then refine it. I also use Git and GitHub to manage the project and track changes throughout development.
answers.weekendScenario:
With 48 hours and a team of three, I’d build an AI Project Copilot that turns meeting notes, requirements, and problem statements into tasks, priorities, deadlines, risks, and decisions.

Users could organize the results into a project board and ask questions based only on their provided information.

I’d use Next.js, React, TypeScript, an LLM API, Supabase, GitHub, and Vercel. One teammate would handle frontend and UX, another the AI and data layer, and the third integration, testing, and deployment.

The goal would be a polished MVP focused on saving users time—not simply adding an LLM.
